To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the percentage of very old patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarctions (MI) increased by almost three-fold in women over the last decade, but by only about 2-fold in men.
the percentage of MI hospitalizations in the United States among very elderly women rose at almost twice (74%) the rate of similarly-aged men between 1997-2006.

the percentage of very old patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarctions rose by 4.9% among women and 2.8% among men between 1997–2006 in the USA, with a significantly higher rate of increase among women.
